claims.text: Machine-learning-aided composition optimization will improve the strength of high-entropy alloys relative to conventionally designed high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning-aided composition optimization will improve the ductility of high-entropy alloys relative to conventionally designed high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning-aided composition optimization will improve Young's modulus relative to conventionally designed high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning-aided composition optimization will improve fracture resistance relative to conventionally designed high-entropy alloys.
The proposed methodology begins with high-entropy alloys in an as-cast state.
Machine learning will be used to design and optimize alloy composition.
The predicted property improvements are conditioned on thermo-mechanical processing and heat treatment.
Short-range order is a structural mediator connecting alloy design and processing to mechanical properties.
Phase decomposition is a structural mediator of the proposed mechanical-property improvements.
Atomic-scale solute engineering and composition optimization provide the mechanism for improving mechanical properties.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for compositions having optimal short-range order and phase decomposition.
The exact relationship between short-range order and mechanical properties is not fully understood.
The exact relationship between phase decomposition and mechanical properties is not fully understood.
The test compares machine-learning-designed alloys against alloys designed without machine learning.
The test will measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation at break, Young's modulus, and fracture toughness.
The hypothesis is falsified if the machine-learning-designed alloys fail to achieve at least a 10% improvement in at least three of the five measured properties.
